text:
The scoreboard said a blowout, and the shot quality mostly agreed. Carolina's 7-2 win over Vancouver at Lenovo Center was effectively settled by the 9:25 mark of the first period, when Andrei Svechnikov scored his second power-play goal and made it 3-0. The Hurricanes finished with 4.70 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.68 and would win 79 percent of simulated replays of every shot. They started it fast: 1.63 expected goals in the first period against 0.49 for the Canucks.

The margin was wider than the play. Carolina's chances were better, but not seven-goals-better. Kevin Lankinen allowed 6 goals on 3.15 expected, a gap of 2.85 goals that turned a clear Carolina edge into a rout. Pyotr Kochetkov, at the other end, was close to par, stopping all but two of 20 shots (2.68 expected). Special teams did the rest. Carolina went 3-for-3 on the power play while Vancouver went 0-for-4, and Logan Stankoven added a short-handed goal in the second period before scoring again on the power play at 19:02. His third, at even strength in the third, gave him a hat trick and made it 7-1. Sean Walker assisted on four goals and played 21:24.

Vancouver's best moments came from Jake DeBrusk, who scored twice on 1.36 individual expected goals, both wrist shots, at 4:03 of the second and 13:04 of the third. Those were the only chances above 40 percent for either side, and they were the two goals Vancouver earned. The Canucks got better as the game went on (0.49, then 1.06, then 1.13 expected goals by period), but by then the lead was too big to chase. Carolina also gave the puck away 26 times to Vancouver's 13 and still won comfortably.
